## Headline

**The raw record is not homogeneous.** Step changes that survive differencing against a neighbouring station were detected in 5 of 12 tested indices (Diurnal temperature range, Rainfall intensity (mm per wet day), Mean wind speed, Mean daily maximum, Hot days (Tmax ≥ 30 °C)). Long-term trends in those variables measure changes in the instrument or its exposure, not the climate, and must not be fed into a phenology model before homogenisation.

Attributed by inference from the diurnal-range break: Mean daily maximum (2002). See the homogeneity section for how attribution works.

Inherited from a broken base variable: Hot days (Tmax ≥ 30 °C) (2002).

Marginal breaks (0.05 ≤ p < 0.10), not disqualifying but worth watching as the record lengthens: Mean temperature (2005), Mean daily minimum (2005), Rain days (≥ 1 mm) (2005).

## What has changed

Theil–Sen slopes with Mann–Kendall significance. Years failing the coverage gate are excluded, so `n` differs between indices.

### Interpretable as climate

- **Mean temperature** — rising, 0.06 °C/decade (0.21 °C over 1991–2025); not significant, n = 28 years.
- **Mean daily minimum** — rising, 0.21 °C/decade (0.72 °C over 1991–2025); marginal, p < 0.10, n = 28 years.
- **Growing degree days (base 10 °C)** — rising, 57.6 °C·d/decade (196 °C·d over 1991–2025); not significant, n = 23 years.
- **Warm season length** — rising, 11.3 days/decade (38.3 days over 1991–2025); marginal, p < 0.10, n = 28 years.
- **Chill days (Tmin ≤ 10 °C)** — falling, 1.3 days/decade (4.3 days over 1991–2025); not significant, n = 28 years.
- **Annual rainfall** — rising, 80.0 mm/decade (272 mm over 1991–2025); not significant, n = 23 years.
- **Rain days (≥ 1 mm)** — falling, 0.7 days/decade (2.4 days over 1991–2025); not significant, n = 23 years.
- **Longest dry spell** — falling, 0.4 days/decade (1.3 days over 1991–2025); not significant, n = 23 years.

### Contaminated by station changes

- **Mean daily maximum** — the 1991–2025 slope of -0.41 °C/decade is **not usable**: a step change at 2002, attributed from the confirmed break in diurnal temperature range, so it reflects the station, not the climate. Within the post-2002 segment alone (19 years) the slope is +0.07 °C/decade (not significant).
- **Diurnal temperature range** — the 1991–2025 slope of -0.68 °C/decade is **not usable**: a step change at 2002 survives differencing against the reference station(s), so it reflects the station, not the climate. Within the post-2002 segment alone (19 years) the slope is -0.32 °C/decade (significant, p < 0.01).
- **Hot days (Tmax ≥ 30 °C)** — the 1991–2025 slope of -6.2 days/decade is **not usable**: it counts days from Mean daily maximum, which breaks at 2002, so it reflects the station, not the climate. Within the post-2002 segment alone (19 years) the slope is +8.9 days/decade (not significant).
- **Rainfall intensity (mm per wet day)** — the 1991–2025 slope of +0.70 mm/d/decade is **not usable**: a step change at 2016 survives differencing against the reference station(s), so it reflects the station, not the climate. Within the post-2016 segment alone (9 years) the slope is -4.24 mm/d/decade (not significant).
- **Mean wind speed** — the 1991–2025 slope of -0.13 m/s/decade is **not usable**: a step change at 2007 survives differencing against the reference station(s), so it reflects the station, not the climate. Within the post-2007 segment alone (15 years) the slope is +0.41 m/s/decade (significant, p < 0.05).

## Homogeneity tests

Pettitt changepoint test. *Direct* runs on the station's own series and will flag real regional climate shifts as well as artificial ones. *vs reference* runs on the difference against a neighbouring station, which cancels regional weather — a break surviving there is a property of this station.
